title: Set up a private home phone network with an agent
summary: A hobbyist bought a secondhand mini cell tower for about 50 CNY and had an AI agent set up the network software; they say it worked almost in one shot.
agent_role: The agent set up and configured the Open5GS core to work with the femtocell. The human bought and supplied the femtocell and eUICC hardware.
outcome: Author reports the agent set up Open5GS with the femtocell in almost one shot.
what_they_did: The poster bought a small home cell tower box (an LTE B40 femtocell) for about 50 CNY on the secondhand site XianYu. They also bought a programmable SIM card for 80 CNY on Taobao. They then had an AI agent set up Open5GS, free software that runs the heart of a mobile network. The result was a private cell network in their home lab.
how_it_went: The author says the setup worked almost in one shot. Next they plan to test how secure phone calling is on their network, and to try fixes for network lag.
worth_knowing: The author says agents let them explore a field outside their PhD topic without much time. The post gives no setup details, so expect to solve problems yourself.
prompt: Help me set up a private LTE network in my home lab using Open5GS and my [femtocell model, band]. First, check what hardware and SIM/eUICC programming I need. Then install and configure Open5GS on [your Linux machine], set the network identifiers to [test PLMN], and connect the femtocell. Show me each config change before applying it. Explain how to verify that a phone attaches. Stay within test-network and local radio regulations.

curation.rationale: An unusual, concrete use: an agent standing up a private LTE core on cheap hardware. But the agent's steps and the result are described in a single sentence.
